$comment: Product Type, split into the values that name a machine and the values that
name a kind of part.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
The hierarchy's Product Type column carries both. For a Corvus 6440 it says
'6440'. For the ribbon that feeds a TTO printer it says 'Ribbon'. Feeding the
column straight into the item's model meant a rep saw 'Model: CIJ Service
Parts' on a part card, and meant a rule keyed to a model could match a word
that is not one.
Rather than guess at build time, the decision is written down here and
reviewed. build_classification.py fails if the hierarchy grows a Product Type
this file does not classify, so the split cannot rot silently as the
catalogue changes.
WHAT COUNTS AS A MODEL
A value is a model if it names the machine the part IS or belongs to:
'6440', 'T400 Series', 'IV18', 'PL6300/LS7100', 'HP 1.0"'. Variants stay
separate ('5400' and '5400 IP65' are different rows) because the difference
is exactly what a specification rule keys on.
A value is a category if it names a kind of part: 'Ribbon', 'Solvents',
'Replacement Parts', 'Installation'. Those parts keep their technology and
their type, and simply have no model.
Print-engine brands ('PALISADE', 'Kestrel', 'Markwell', 'Printronix', 'Tharo') are
categories here. They name who made the engine inside a label applicator,
not the Axim machine being quoted.
Five values name a machine family with no digit in the string, so no rule
about the shape of the text could find them. They were promoted by hand
after reading the hierarchy: UJ, UJ II, T200, Alphacoder, SolidJet.
Values not confidently either way stay categories. 'FASA', 'WASA', 'HST',
'LELA', 'Jaguar' and 'Apollo' may well be product families, but promoting a
value on a hunch would put a wrong model on a quote, so they wait for someone
who knows.
MODELS THE HIERARCHY DOES NOT NAME
"extraModels" holds machines that are quoted and documented but that the
Product Type column has no value for. The Ridgeline 3200 is the case that
found this: seventeen parts name 'Mark 2', 'Mark 4' or 'Ridgeline 3200' in
their descriptions, Axim publishes a technical datasheet for it, and
every one of those parts still landed under a Product Type of 'Replacement
Parts' or 'Accessories'. Without this list its datasheet figures could not
reach a quote.
Add a value here only when the machine is real and a document says so.
The PALM entries are the three apply modules Axim publishes a product
page for: axim-e-tamp-module, axim-e-fasa-swing-arm-apply-module and
axim-corner-wrap-labeling-e-wasa. 'FASA' and 'WASA' stay categories above
because those bare values name a family with no generation; 'E-FASA' names the
all-electric module the page describes.
The print-engine model numbers stamped into the descriptions — PE311, PE321,
K84X, K86X — are deliberately NOT here. They are Palisade and Kestrel engines, and
the rule above is that a model needs a document; Axim publishes no
datasheet for them, so there is nothing a specification rule could cite.
Which attributes name the MACHINE, per technology.
The CIJ price page lists one row per orderable SKU, and a Corvus SKU is a
printer already filled: Printer Type x Printhead Type x Ink x Color. Nine
printers, six printheads and forty-eight inks come to 947 rows, so "which
machine" was answered with a list of 947 and a rep scrolling six at a time.
The machine is the printer. The printhead length and angle, the ink and its
colour are how it is filled - real decisions, made after you know which
machine, and made against the application rather than by scrolling. So the
list groups on the keys named here and the rest become the choice inside a
group, which still resolves to one real orderable part number.
A technology absent from this map is not grouped: TTO, PALM, PIJ and TIJ
list one row per machine already, which is what a machine list should be.
Product Type -> a more exact type than the Product Line gives.
'CIJ Consumables' maps to consumable, which is true of all 311 parts under
it and not very useful: 149 of them are inks, 90 are solvents, 50 are
CombiPaks and 22 are filter kits, and the hierarchy says so in the Product
Type column. The classification vocabulary already had an ink type and a
printhead type, and nothing in the pipeline ever produced either — so two of
the ten filters on the Classify screen returned nothing, every time.
Only where the Product Type names a KIND of part. Where it names a machine
(6420, 5400 IP65) it is the model and is left alone — see $comment above.
E-TAMP, E-FASA and E-WASA are apply modules, not machines. REPORTED: "E-TAMP is
not a machine it is the applicator for the labels in PALM." They stay MODELS —
Axim publishes a product page for each and a rule may need to name one — and
they stop being printers, so they no longer appear in the machine list of a PALM
quote. The maintenance kits under the same Product Type keep being spares: the
description-based narrowing runs after this and still says so.
